headline: US Warns of Mass-Casualty Attack in Moscow on Saturday
caption:
The US warned of a mass-casualty attack at Moscow's Tsaritsyno on Saturday, and Russia's Federal Security Service said the US tipped it off. Washington gave a similar warning weeks before the 2024 Crocus City Hall attack that killed over 100. Neither government has named a suspect or said whether anyone is in custody.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Rubio Sees Growing Interest in a Black Sea Ceasefire
caption:
US Secretary of State Rubio says interest is growing in a Black Sea ceasefire, as the US reviews Turkish and Indian proposals to halt attacks on grain ships and, in some cases, energy cargoes. Ukraine and Russia, both major wheat exporters, are now attacking each other's ships, and Canada's foreign minister said Russia has not shown it is willing to move ahead.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: FBI Blames North Korea for $6.3 Billion Binance Theft
caption:
The FBI says North Korea's TraderTraitor group stole $6.3 billion from Binance and is now moving the funds into Ethereum. Bitcoin fell about 5% after the theft, and the FBI has asked exchanges to block transactions linked to the suspect wallets.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Qatari LNG carrier struck near Hormuz amid Iran-US talks
caption:
Qatar Gas Transport Company said unidentified objects struck its LNG carrier Al Mayeda on Friday evening, causing no injuries, and the vessel remains operational. People with direct knowledge say Pakistan had negotiated Iranian safe passage for the ship beforehand, and the company's statement names no attacker.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Adviser Warns Retaliation Will Reach Beyond West Asia
caption:
Iran will retaliate beyond West Asia, state news agency Mehr reported, citing Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Ayatollah Khamenei, and Russia's TASS carried the same post. Mehr said Khamenei told commanders on Saturday to prepare a response with no geographic limits, while neither report names a weapon, a range or a target.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ukraine claims record 54,400 Russian casualties in October
caption:
Ukraine's General Staff says Russia lost 54,400 soldiers killed, wounded or missing in October, a monthly record, in a count Kyiv itself compiled. President Zelensky said Ukraine retook 37 square miles while Russia reportedly took 33, and that only a Russian ceasefire would stop the losses.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Netanyahu Urges Trump to Strike Iran After Midterms
caption:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing President Donald Trump to strike Iran after the US midterm elections, sources say, as the White House weighs renewed combat while Qatari-mediated talks continue. Trump said the US could hit the suspected nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain "in 10 minutes," while Iran's foreign minister says no agreement exists yet.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Rioters Injure Over 100 Police in Frankfurt
caption:
Rioters injured more than 100 of 1,300 police deployed at a Frankfurt youth protest over education and living costs, with 54 arrested, 17 stores damaged and 5 looted, Hesse's interior minister said. Germany's ministers promise severe penalties, while Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed immigrant-community troublemakers without evidence, though most of those arrested were German nationals.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Cyberattacks heat freezers to 50°C in dozens of European supermarkets
caption:
Freezers in dozens of European supermarkets reached 50°C overnight in an apparent cyberattack, and a Belgian butcher says it ruined €15,000 of meat. Sabcobel's chief executive says attackers switched evaporators to defrost mode, while Carrefour Belgium says only 15 of its 700 stores were affected.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Cuts Hormuz Reopening Offer From 7 Days to 2
caption:
Iran has cut its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz from 7 days to 2, conditional on the US ending its blockade of Iranian ports, unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the war on all fronts. US and Israeli military officials are drafting plans for renewed strikes after the 3 November midterms.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Generic HIV prevention shot to cost $40 a year, not $28,218
caption:
Generic lenacapavir, the twice-yearly HIV prevention shot, is expected to cost $40 a year instead of $28,218 after the US FDA tentatively approved India's Dr. Reddy's Laboratories version. It opens supply to 120 low- and middle-income countries, though generics from other licensed makers still await approval and some countries require national sign-off first.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Midterms become a vote on Trump’s Iran war
caption:
Diesel hit a record $6.52 a gallon in September as the Iran war pushed up fuel prices, putting cost of living at the center of midterm races that will decide control of the Senate. Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats, with contests in Michigan, Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Alaska and North Carolina.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: North Korea denies stealing $6.3bn from Binance
caption:
Kim Yo-jong denied that North Korea stole $6.3bn from Binance, the largest crypto theft on record, which the FBI attributes to Pyongyang's TraderTraitor group. President Trump told reporters in Florida, "We don't know if it's North Korea," and US investigators have yet to publish their forensics.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers set fridges to 50C across seven European countries
caption:
Suspected hackers set commercial fridges to 50C across 7 European countries, and UK meat suppliers lost stock, though a National Cyber Security Centre official calls the impact minimal. Researchers found more than 800 refrigeration and building-control interfaces exposed to the public internet, and no group has claimed responsibility.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump says $4 billion in Israel military aid ends at year-end
caption:
Trump says $4 billion in US aid to Israel will stop at year-end, though Congress appropriates the money and a 10-year memorandum signed in 2016 runs through 2028. Netanyahu's office has not responded, and a Chicago Council poll found 68% of Republicans favour continuing aid.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Demands Recognition of Hormuz Sovereignty in Five Conditions
caption:
Iran demands recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, plus sanctions relief, war reparations and a guarantee against future attack, in terms that exceed what mediators seek, Tasnim reported. Armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi's plan goes beyond the proposed swap of an end to Hormuz attacks for a lifted US blockade.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Greenland’s parliament approves US security deal 16-0
caption:
Greenland's parliament passed a US security deal 16-0 with 7 abstentions, expanding US operations at Pituffik Space Base and keeping them in place even if Greenland becomes independent. The deal takes effect only after Denmark ratifies it, with Danish lawmakers set to debate it later this month.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Democrats flip 6 Senate seats and win the House
caption:
Democrats flipped 6 Senate seats and won the House, gaining subpoena power over the Trump administration for the final two years of his term. President Donald Trump said of the losses, "I think a part of it was Iran," as AP polling found 4 in 10 voters ranked the economy first, citing petrol prices that rose after the Iran war began.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Abdul El-Sayed Becomes America’s First Muslim Senator
caption:
Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race to become the first Muslim in the US Senate, while Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man elected to the chamber. Keisha Lance Bottoms and Deb Haaland also won governorships in Georgia and New Mexico, as the first Black woman and first Native American woman to lead those states, and Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first Black House speaker when Democrats take control in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers tried to overheat French blood bank plasma storage
caption:
Attackers targeted the refrigeration control systems at 3 French blood-storage sites in an attempt to push plasma temperatures past boiling, but the French Blood Establishment says no products were lost and distribution never stopped. Monitoring alarms flagged the anomalies, and the cybersecurity agency and Health Ministry are investigating without naming a suspect.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Israel displaces nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron in 11 days
caption:
Israel's army displaced nearly 5,000 Palestinians from Hebron in 11 days, sealing the city's entrances and disrupting schooling for 80,000 students. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the army is prepared for an extensive operation across the West Bank.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hubert Aiwanger, 55, found dead in Berlin hotel room
caption:
Hubert Aiwanger, 55, leader of the Free Voters and deputy to Bavarian Minister-President Markus Soeder, was found dead in a Berlin hotel room. Police sources say the cause appears health-related with no sign of foul play, and prosecutors have opened an inquest.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Joshua Wong’s release pushed back nine years, to 2036
caption:
Hong Kong court extends Joshua Wong's jail term by nearly a decade, moving his release from January 2027 to November 2036 after a conviction for lobbying foreign governments for sanctions. Judge William Tam set 13 years as the starting point, then cut 3 for Wong's September guilty plea.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Another tanker hits a mine east of Hormuz
caption:
Another tanker hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy says, in a waterway that normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption and that Iran calls closed to uncoordinated ships. The navy said the vessel had switched off its tracking systems.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Paraguay’s president resigns after bank serving 60% of adults collapses
caption:
Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigned Thursday, hours after regulators seized Ueno Bank, which counted 60% of the country's adults as customers. Prosecutors have charged 27 Ueno officials, and insured deposits of up to $38,000 per person must be paid within 15 days.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Newsom commutes all 548 California death sentences
caption:
Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted all 548 death sentences in California, home to the Western Hemisphere's largest death row, to life in prison on Thursday. Victims' advocates say they will challenge the commutations in court.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Arabia’s $5 billion LIV Golf bet ends in liquidation
caption:
Saudi Arabia's $5 billion LIV Golf venture is being liquidated after a $300 million BC Partners rescue collapsed when top players, including Dustin Johnson and Bryson DeChambeau, declined to sign. Seven executives received $15.6 million before the 8 September bankruptcy filing, including CEO Scott O'Neil's $6.375 million.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Judge Freezes Trump’s Arch Hours After Approval
caption:
A US judge has frozen construction of Trump's 250-foot arch in Washington for 14 days, hours after the planning commission approved it 8-4. The National Park Service says the arch could harm as many as 42 historic sites.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: South Korea halts trading as Kospi plunges 8%
caption:
South Korea halted trading Friday after the Kospi fell 8%, as the AI-driven selloff spread across Asia and Taiwan's benchmark lost 12.2% this week. Cleanview data show 40% of pending US data-centre capacity sits in states whose new Democratic governors promised pauses.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: $1.26 billion in crypto bets wiped out as Bitcoin falls below $75,000
caption:
Bitcoin fell below $75,000 for the first time since 15 September as the Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, and CoinGlass says $1.26 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $430.2 million Thursday, SoSoValue data show.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Stephen Miller to run the White House from Monday
caption:
President Trump named Stephen Miller, the architect of his deportation policy, White House chief of staff to replace Susie Wiles, effective Monday, after the midterm defeat. Miller previously set US immigration agents a target of 3,000 arrests a day, and Democrats, who take both chambers in January, are expected to investigate him.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Three Ships Sunk in a Week in the Strait of Hormuz
caption:
Three ships sank in the Strait of Hormuz in 7 days, and UK Maritime Trade Operations counted 11 attacks through 4 November, 8 in the strait and 3 in the Arabian Gulf. A projectile strike on a dhow on 2 November killed 1 crew member.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US offers up to $20 million for tips on Iran’s nuclear program
caption:
The US State Department is offering up to $20 million and relocation to informants on Iran's nuclear program, saying Iran's non-compliance cost the UN nuclear watchdog track of its centrifuge production and inventory. Senior US officials point to the moonless night of 9 November as Trump weighs renewed strikes.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US projectiles hit Iran’s Qeshm island again
caption:
Two US projectiles struck Iran's Qeshm island Friday night, as UK maritime monitors log at least 11 ships attacked near Hormuz in a week, 3 of them sunk. Iran's navy said a tanker with its transponder off hit a mine and caught fire in the eastern strait, while Washington says the mines were cleared.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunman kills six in Kraków’s Main Square
caption:
A gunman who drove into Kraków's Main Square and fired at random from his car killed 6 people, police said. Officers gave conflicting accounts on whether he had accomplices, and no motive has been given.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US aircraft fires on cargo ship leaving Iran
caption:
US Central Command says its blockade of Iran now extends to the country's land borders and the Caspian Sea, after a US aircraft fired on a cargo ship leaving Iran. A new 20-person task force in Tampa will coordinate efforts on weapons, dual-use goods and revenue.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Two tankers burn after hitting mines in Hormuz
caption:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 2 tankers are burning after hitting mines in and east of the Strait of Hormuz, and warn any ship leaving Iran's authorised route will strike a mine. The Guards named neither ship, and no outside party has confirmed the mines.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Europe’s largest nuclear plant runs on diesel generators
caption:
Europe's largest nuclear plant, Zaporizhzhia, is running on diesel generators after losing its last working 330 kV power line, its 16th complete blackout of 2026, Energoatom said. Energoatom says Russia is deliberately disabling the lines, while the plant's own report names no cause, and warns fuel cooling is at risk if the generators fail or run out of fuel.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russian strikes cut power to 850,000 people
caption:
Russian strikes cut power to about 850,000 people in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, energy provider DTEK said, as repeated attacks slow repairs ahead of winter. Russia's defence ministry said it will keep striking energy sites it says aid Ukraine's army.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Egypt train collision kills 7, injures 112
caption:
Egypt's Health Ministry says 7 people died and 112 were injured when a Giza-to-Fayoum train rammed the rear of a Cairo-to-Aswan service in al-Ayyat, derailing carriages onto a road. Al-Ayyat is where more than 370 people died in Egypt's worst rail disaster, a 2002 train fire.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump holds 38 Iranian bridges at risk as talks open
caption:
Trump holds 38 Iranian bridges at risk, tying restraint to a nuclear deal and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as an Iraqi delegation spent 8 hours in Tehran delivering a US message, unnamed sources said. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Washington must choose between a deal and war.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump vows comeback after midterm loss as Miller becomes chief of staff
caption:
Democrats have won both chambers of Congress, with the Senate count at 54 to 44, gaining power to summon officials, demand documents and hold hearings. Incoming oversight chair Robert Garcia plans to question Elon Musk and Stephen Miller, the new White House chief of staff, in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 20 Migrants Dead Off Crete, 12 Bodies Pulled From One Boat
caption:
Greece's coast guard says 20 migrants have died trying to reach Crete in recent days, including 12 bodies recovered from one boat off Kali Limenes. Frontex rescued 87 more people from two boats about 56 kilometres south of the port.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Viktor Orbán’s brother detained in Hungary raids
caption:
Police in Hungary have reportedly detained Áron Orbán, brother of Viktor Orbán, in raids tied to a probe into a network that allegedly sold work visas to foreigners. Viktor Orbán calls the case political, saying "I am the target, my younger brother is just a tool."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 16 workers killed in Turkish steel plant explosion
caption:
16 workers were killed and 13 injured at the Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, Turkey, after a ceiling crane collapsed into an electric arc furnace and damaged a natural gas line, the governor said. President Erdoğan said 4 prosecutors have been assigned, and the mayor says the final toll awaits cleared debris.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline set ablaze in unclaimed attack
caption:
An unclaimed attack set fire to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the kingdom's main crude export route since the US-Israeli war closed the Strait of Hormuz. The energy ministry said operations were unaffected and no one was hurt.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump Holds Iran Strikes After Gulf Allies Ask
caption:
President Trump is holding off on new strikes on Iran after Gulf neighbours asked him to, while Israel's Netanyahu presses him daily to resume, a briefed person said. Iran offers free Hormuz shipping if the US lifts its port blockade, frees frozen assets and restarts final-deal talks.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran hacked freezers in 700 French supermarkets, prosecutors say
caption:
France says Iran's Revolutionary Guards heated freezers in 700 French supermarkets, which prosecutors call the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot summoned Iran's ambassador and is seeking EU sanctions, which need all 27 member states to agree.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 1,000 TikTok abuse videos drew 48 million views
caption:
Spain's youth ministry is weighing a TikTok suspension and has asked prosecutors to act, after fact-checkers Maldita.es reported 1,000 abuse videos drew 48 million views. Maldita.es says TikTok's algorithm recommended 19 livestreams by minors in 3 days.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Sets Seven Conditions for Talks, Denies Any US Contact
caption:
Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the US meets 7 conditions, and that Washington has given no clear response, security official Mohsen Rezaei told Al-Mayadeen. President Trump rejected Iran's truce plan after meeting mediator Qatar on Monday, while playing down a return to war.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 11 dead in Bulgaria motorway fog pile-ups
caption:
Two fog-related pile-ups near Yambol, Bulgaria, killed 11 people and injured dozens, as visibility fell from 70-80 metres to about 10 within minutes, the interior minister said. Officials said drivers were going too fast, and the government wants Wednesday as a day of national mourning.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: House shelves Hegseth impeachment 211 to 204
caption:
The House voted 211 to 204 to shelve the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, with 11 Democrats, including Nancy Pelosi, skipping a committee-referral vote that 8 of them could have defeated. Democrats take control of Congress in January and can try again, and Republican Thomas Massie, the only Republican backing impeachment, said of the Republicans opposed, "They know it's a sinking ship but committed to stay on board."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia detains two Polish intelligence agents in Kaliningrad
caption:
Russia's Federal Security Service says it detained 2 Polish intelligence agents in Kaliningrad and issued warnings to 7 Poles and 3 Russians over alleged espionage and treason. Officials allege the group gathered data on military sites and migration policy for Polish military intelligence, and a court has jailed both agents while the cases proceed.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Three tankers hit mines as Hormuz stays shut
caption:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran says the strait stays shut until Washington answers its 7 conditions, with monitoring firms counting 37 attacks on ships nearby in November, the most in any month of the war. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says it could reopen within 2 days if the demands are met.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: At least 7 US officials moved from their homes for protection, Bessent to a mili
caption:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved onto a military base after alleged threats from Iran, one of at least 7 US officials who have left their homes for protection. A person familiar with the matter said media reports identifying his home address contributed to the move, and Iran has repeatedly denied plotting attacks on US soil.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia’s ambassador to the US, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
caption:
Alexander Darchiev, 66, Russia's ambassador to the United States since March 2025, has died, the Russian foreign ministry said. Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova cited a chronic illness, though the ministry's statement said only that he died suddenly.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: First Democrat to win Mississippi’s Senate seat since 1982
caption:
Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's Senate seat, the first Democratic win there since 1982, defeating Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by a few thousand votes after a count that took more than a week. He will be the state's first Black senator in more than 140 years and gives Democrats 55 Senate seats, with Alaska uncalled.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Netanyahu presses Trump almost daily to resume striking Iran
caption:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing President Trump almost daily to resume strikes on Iran, and one call became a shouting match as Trump insisted on diplomacy, sources told Israel's Ynet. Netanyahu's office confirmed the call but denied it was confrontational.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Starshield cuts off Ukrainian drones above 161 km/h, Zelensky says
caption:
Zelensky says Starshield is again cutting off Ukrainian military connections above 161 km/h, leaving interceptors unable to reach Russian jet-powered drones in time, and some strikes got through. The military says the limit is systematic and follows an October cap lifted on 24 October.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Colette Kress takes over
caption:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, president and director after more than 30 years, and finance chief Colette Kress now runs the company. Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after reports linked Huang to a businesswoman US authorities reportedly suspect of Chinese intelligence ties.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Microsoft outage logs 130,000 Outlook reports worldwide
caption:
Microsoft Outlook, Teams and Copilot failed in 74 countries within an hour, with Downdetector logging 130,000 Outlook outage reports at the peak. Microsoft says servers failing automated health checks went offline and the strain on the rest caused the overload; it has not found a recent change coinciding with the start and has not said when service fully returns.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump Says He Would Consider Military Force Against Cuba
caption:
President Trump says he would consider military force against Cuba, which the US has blockaded of oil since January, with the island's power grid repeatedly collapsing. Cuba's foreign minister called the G7's position "false arguments fabricated by Washington," and Southern Command told senators in March it was not rehearsing an invasion.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: ICE deports a record 483,200 people in fiscal 2026
caption:
US immigration agents deported a record 483,200 people in fiscal 2026, up from the previous record of 442,640 in 2025, according to Department of Homeland Security figures. Researcher Steven Camarota says the data does not separate interior removals from people turned back at borders or airports.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia’s October oil revenue jumps 65% to $21.2 billion
caption:
Russia's oil export revenue rose 65% to $21.2 billion in October, its highest monthly total since May, as the Iran war lifted prices, the International Energy Agency said. Gulf exports excluding Oman remain 26% below prewar levels as attacks on Hormuz tankers continue.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Turkey signs second mutual defence pact with Qatar since August
caption:
Turkey and Qatar are to work together to prevent renewed war in the Gulf, President Erdogan said, as Turkey signs its 2nd mutual defence pact since August. Erdogan's office gave no terms, so what each side owes the other is unknown.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: FAA halts every departing flight across the US
caption:
Every departing flight in the US was stopped Friday after a communication fault hit all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, and inbound international flights are landing only case by case. Two law enforcement officials said preliminary reports indicate it was not a cyberattack, and the FAA has not named a cause or said when departures resume.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US asks Ukraine to give up Donbas for NATO entry
caption:
Zelensky says the US has asked Ukraine to give up the rest of Donbas, where Russia holds about 88% of the territory, in exchange for a path to NATO membership. Any deal would go to a national referendum, he said; the Kremlin has not responded.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Mossad warned US of explosive drones aimed at Trump
caption:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said President Trump and his family are Iran's top target, after Mossad reportedly warned the US of explosive drones aimed at Trump. Mullin said much of the intelligence amounts to chatter, though officials treat every threat at face value, and sources say Trump may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes after liftoff, 40 Amazon satellites lost
caption:
United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed to deliver all 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit on Sunday, 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, ending the company's 100% success record. ULA says it has no data on the cause, and investigators could ground Vulcan for months.

Amazon Leo has 398 satellites in orbit, 12% of the 3,236 it needs.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet Thursday without Ukraine or Europe
caption:
Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen on 19 November without Ukraine, Europe or Japan present, even as US officials say Trump will raise nuclear arms and Iran rather than Ukraine. China has long insisted the US and Russia cut their arsenals before it discusses its own, and a Tsinghua University professor says Xi is unlikely to negotiate nuclear terms Thursday.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: EU clears UniCredit’s €45 billion Commerzbank takeover
caption:
The EU gave unconditional approval to UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank, and competition chief Teresa Ribera warned the Commission will act if Germany tries to block it. Berlin, which holds about 12% of Commerzbank, is demanding job guarantees, a Frankfurt headquarters and two supervisory board seats.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Cuts Hormuz Reopening Plan From 7 Days to 2
caption:
Iran has shortened its proposed Strait of Hormuz reopening plan from 7 days to 2, Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said after talks with Iran's Abbas Araghchi in Islamabad. Dar said Washington has yet to respond and hopes it will answer very soon, after its midterm elections.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Wheat ship capsizes off Bulgaria after reported sea-drone strike
caption:
A Somali-flagged ship carrying 3,000 metric tons of wheat from Romania to Egypt sank off Bulgaria in a reported sea-drone strike, and all 12 crew survived. Betul 8 is the 17th vessel attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July, security firm Diaplous says.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Third US Carrier Joins 13 Destroyers Facing Iran
caption:
A third US aircraft carrier, the Roosevelt, has reached the Persian Gulf, putting 3 carriers and 13 destroyers opposite Iran, a defence official said, giving Trump more options to restart strikes. The Roosevelt joins two carriers enforcing a blockade that has redirected 150 merchant ships since June, US Central Command says.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Mongolia’s president to resign over $25 million bribery allegation
caption:
Mongolia's President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh will resign over an allegation by former Ulaanbaatar mayor Nyambaatar Khishgee that he received $25 million in bribes tied to a 2019 railway contract awarded without tender to Bodi International. Khurelsukh and Bodi deny wrongdoing, and parliament votes on the resignation this week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Hits Bahrain With Third Drone Attack in a Week
caption:
Iran launched its third drone attack on Bahrain in a week, with the Revolutionary Guard saying it targeted a radar at the US-used Sheikh Isa air base, while US Central Command says every drone was intercepted. Qatar says mediation continues, but talks remain stalled and the US blockade of Iranian ports stands.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia strikes 2 Kyiv bridges and the subway, cutting water and power
caption:
Russia struck 2 Kyiv bridges and the subway, partly cutting water and power, and Ukraine answered by hitting the Kerch Bridge, the only link between Crimea and southern Russia. A Ukrainian drone attack killed at least 2 people in Crimea, the Moscow-installed governor said, and bridge traffic is suspended.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Nvidia doubles profit to $65.3 billion, forecasts $130bn quarter
caption:
Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion against $109 billion expected, doubled profit to $65.3 billion and guided $130 billion for next quarter, a forecast that excludes China data-centre sales. Shares have fallen more than 36% in the past month, and the 10-Q filing will come weeks late.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pentagon Says Ukraine’s Deep Strikes Failed; Germany and UK Disagree
caption:
Germany and Britain publicly rejected Pentagon official Elbridge Colby's claim that Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia have failed, opening a split among Ukraine's backers. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius called the criticism "quite a stupid thing" and cited Russia's nightly strikes on Ukrainian heating.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Peltola Flips Alaska as Democrats Reach 56 Senate Seats
caption:
Mary Peltola defeated Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska with 50.1% of first-choice votes to his 45.8%, vote counts show, lifting Democrats to 56 Senate seats after nine flips. That is still short of the two-thirds needed to override a Trump veto.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth
caption:
Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth, so a command sent to the probe takes 24 hours to arrive, farther than any other human-made object has travelled at about 26 billion kilometres. Its power falls by about 4 watts a year, and engineers have switched off its cameras and all but 2 of 10 instruments; a Jet Propulsion Laboratory spokesperson says power could last 3 to 4 more years.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Salvadoran helicopters fire missiles on Haitian gang stronghold
caption:
Salvadoran helicopters fired missiles at another Haitian gang stronghold, President Nayib Bukele said, after El Salvador sent 2,000-plus troops to Haiti, where the UN recorded 4,595 killings in the year's first 10 months. The UN human rights office urged all forces on Tuesday to use lethal force only as a last resort.

headline: US signs military pact with Venezuela 10 months after capturing Maduro
caption:
The US signed a military pact with Venezuela's acting government 10 months after capturing Nicolás Maduro, covering joint training and intelligence sharing, while promised elections remain unscheduled. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the deal requires defence reforms inside Venezuela's military, and the Pentagon has not released the agreement's text.

headline: Houthi missile debris falls on Riyadh
caption:
Debris from a Houthi missile fell on Riyadh, and the coalition reported material damage, while Houthi forces advance on Aden, the temporary capital of Yemen's recognised government. The Saudi-led coalition says it struck 60 Houthi targets, and Polymarket traders now give a Saudi-Houthi ceasefire by 31 December a 9% chance, down 18 points in a week.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Islam set to overtake Christianity as largest religion by 2035
caption:
Pew Research projects Muslims will outnumber Christians by 2035, at 2.57 billion against 2.52 billion, as the largest religion in the world. Pew attributes the shift to Muslim women averaging 3.1 children against 2.5 for Christian women, and to Islam losing fewer members to religious switching.

headline: GTA VI sells 17 million copies, earning $1.65 billion at launch
caption:
Grand Theft Auto VI has sold 17 million copies and earned an estimated $1.65 billion, according to Sensor Tower, lifting shares of Take-Two, Sony and Microsoft. About 75% of sales are on PlayStation 5, and the game cost an estimated $1 billion to make.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Anthropic Raises Record $81.3bn in Nasdaq Debut
caption:
Anthropic raised a record $81.3bn in its Nasdaq listing at an $83 offering price, with each of its 7 co-founders holding a stake worth about $20bn, company-filing estimates show. The prospectus discloses a $104bn net loss in the first nine months of 2026 and $900.9bn in long-term infrastructure commitments.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Four men convicted of raping drugged Joanne Young
caption:
A jury in Winchester convicted 4 men of raping Joanne Young, who was drugged by her then-husband Philip Young, in England's first conviction for organised drug-facilitated sexual assault. The men said they believed she consented, but she was heavily sedated, and the National Crime Agency has identified more than 270 people linked to one online forum and its successors.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers Breach Data at JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard
caption:
A breach at one unnamed vendor exposed customer names, email addresses and phone numbers at JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard, the companies said. Visa says its systems were untouched and no card numbers were affected, and none of the three has named the vendor or said how many customers were hit.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Suspected Russian missile burns in a Polish field
caption:
A suspected Russian projectile burned in a field in Chmielek, Poland, 60 miles from British and allied troops training for a postwar Ukraine mission. Ukrainian monitors tracked a KH-101 cruise missile toward Poland, while a central administration source told Onet it was likely a drone.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Malaysia to send 10,000 Rohingya refugees to Turkey
caption:
Malaysia will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey, Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said, with 3 to 6 months of vocational training for Turkish jobs. No start date has been announced, and Turkey's foreign ministry has not responded.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Wants Ukraine Peace Deal by January 2027
caption:
The US wants a Ukraine peace deal by January 2027, officials say, and Kushner said Russia appears ready to accept guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5. Zelensky said he is unsure Ukraine and the US share one understanding of such guarantees, and a Ukrainian official fears Kyiv will be pushed toward Moscow's terms before Democrats take Congress.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Denmark expels Russian attaché over hired-gang assassination plot
caption:
Denmark has given a Russian attaché 7 days to leave after Danish intelligence said Russia hired a gang to kill Kyivstoner, what it calls the first known Russian assassination attempt on Danish soil. Two men face attempted murder charges and deny the allegations.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers reach FBI database US police use for warrants
caption:
Hackers reportedly breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the database US police query for warrants, which also holds records on crime victims, missing people and people under court protection. Investigators have not said whether records were copied or altered, or who is responsible.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunfire empties Sinaloa ballpark after Chapo Isidro arrest
caption:
Gunfire emptied a ballpark and burning trucks blocked highways into Guasave, a Sinaloa city of about 300,000, as Mexican media report soldiers seized Chapo Isidro, a fugitive wanted in the US since 2012. Authorities have not officially confirmed the arrest.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Two missiles and a drone fall on southeast Poland
caption:
2 missiles and a drone fell on southeast Poland, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation by Russia timed to nearby European military exercises. Article 5 needs agreement from all 32 NATO members, so Poland can only invoke Article 4, which triggers consultations.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Nasdaq falls 5.28% in a day, erasing all 2026 gains
caption:
The Nasdaq fell 5.28% on Friday, erasing all of its 2026 gains, as the 7 biggest tech stocks lost more than $4 trillion in 6 weeks, Bloomberg data show. The European Central Bank has warned that circular ownership links obscure the risk.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: COP31 Draft Deal Drops Fossil Fuels Entirely
caption:
COP31's draft climate deal in Antalya no longer mentions fossil fuels, after talks ran 24 hours over, while about 130 countries want the transition acknowledged, Ireland's climate minister said. Saudi Arabia leads opposition to a phase-out, and the EU prefers no deal to a bad one.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Congress wins 27 of 37 Rajasthan district councils
caption:
Congress won 27 of Rajasthan's 37 district councils and 269 of 419 block-level Panchayat Samitis, defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party, which took 6 councils and 73 samitis. The BJP's state president conceded, and counting in Kota, Sri Ganganagar, Baran and Karauli takes place on 17 December.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hegseth Restricts US Military Cooperation With Canada
caption:
US officials say Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has restricted US military cooperation with Canada under a classified memo, which the Pentagon says refocuses the relationship on American defence priorities. Canada's defence minister says he has not seen the memo and sees no change in cooperation, and neither government has said which programmes are covered.
